document_summary: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78.016 bans non-refundable fees charged to existing tenants for renewing a tenancy or changing roommates, while preserving tenant screening fees allowed under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (Berkeley, CA).

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-refundable Application Fees Associated with Existing Tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners and their agents may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate. Screening fees permitted under Civ. Code § 1950.6 may still be charged, including to a new or additional roommate.
rules.key_value: Ban on non-refundable renewal/roommate-change fees for existing tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents; protects existing tenants and households.
rules.exemptions: Tenant screening fees permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 are not disallowed, including for a new or additional roommate seeking to be added to an existing lease.
rules.interaction: Works alongside the state screening-fee cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6, which this ordinance expressly preserves.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for an owner of residential rental property or the owner's agent to charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.conflict_note: The permitted screening fee is governed by Civ. Code § 1950.6, which has no single official 2026 dollar figure. The figure is not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: The history note gives only 'Ord. 7697-NS § 1, 2020', with no adoption or effective date, so both dates are null. This is a code-publisher capture of the municipal code.
